Repo: /opt/nxeon-v2, branch design/v2 — a from-scratch visual redesign ("Nexion") of the real Nxeon hosting platform, running sandboxed (NXEON_SANDBOX=1: real database, real code paths, but no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged). Read /opt/nxeon-v2/CLAUDE.md FIRST — it has non-negotiable rules for this tree, the most important for you being: "Never fabricate. No invented stats, capabilities, or UI implying something the backend doesn't actually do. If a number/capability cannot be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why." Read docs/NEXION-V2.md too for design-direction context. Login: customer@nxeon.local / wGPZqhCbsLdz (also in /root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt), base URL https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud.

CRITICAL CONCURRENCY WARNING — read before running anything: other agents may be working in this same tree concurrently. `./rebuild.sh` temporarily renames `app/(marketing)` to `app/_marketing_skipped` during a build (to skip compiling it) and renames it back after — this is normally safe because the script takes a real `flock` on `/tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock` and simply refuses to run (printing "another rebuild is already running") if one is already in progress, rather than blocking or corrupting anything. A prior incident this session happened because an agent got confused seeing `app/_marketing_skipped` mid-build (from ANOTHER process's in-flight rebuild) and manually deleted or manipulated it, thinking it was disposable — that destroyed the entire marketing site until it was restored from git. DO NOT ever manually touch, rename, delete, or "clean up" `app/(marketing)` or `app/_marketing_skipped` yourself for any reason. Just call `./rebuild.sh` normally; if it says another rebuild is already running, wait a bit (don't poll a lockfile's mere existence — that file is never deleted, only the flock on it matters) and just try `./rebuild.sh` again later. Never touch git commits — the orchestrating session commits everyone's work together.

YOUR TASK, verbatim from the user (a lot of detail here — read all of it before starting):

---
Now let's move on to the Shared Hosting Dashboard.

The current Shared Hosting Dashboard is cluttered, poorly organized, redundant, and missing important functionality. I want to completely restructure and clean it up while using the existing VPS Dashboard styling as the visual foundation.

Do not change the overall Nxeon design language. Keep the same premium dark UI, blue/purple accents, glowing borders, modern cards, spacing, typography, and interactive elements used throughout the VPS Dashboard.

## HERO SECTION
The hero should have a large website preview/image on the left.
- Initially use a cloud-hosting placeholder image.
- Once the system detects the customer's main website, automatically replace the placeholder with a screenshot of the website's homepage.
- The screenshot should be automatically scraped by the system.
- Allow the customer to optionally upload a custom thumbnail instead of using the placeholder or scraped screenshot.

Beside the image, show: Hosting plan name, exact plan/tag they're subscribed to, main website domain, PHP version, hosting status, plan/resource information. The hero should also include an Upgrade Plan button.

The resource metrics should clearly show both the current usage and the plan limit, for example: Websites — 2 / 10, Storage — 25 GB / 100 GB, Bandwidth — 200 GB / 1 TB, Email Accounts — 4 / 25, Databases — 2 / 10. Make the usage visually obvious without making the hero feel overloaded.

## MAIN TABS
Below the hero, create these tabs: Overview, Websites, Files, Databases, Backups, Activity, Settings, Email, Apps, Cron.

## OVERVIEW
Clean summary of the entire hosting plan without unnecessary duplication. Include:

### Websites Card
Large card, grid of all websites attached to the hosting plan (2x3 or 3x2 depending on count). Each website card: thumbnail, domain/subdomain, website status, installed application icons, "View More". Thumbnail can be: auto-scraped screenshot, custom uploaded thumbnail, or placeholder. Show application icons for installed apps (WordPress, Joomla, etc); if none installed show an appropriate empty/placeholder state. Include an empty dotted-grid card at the end with "Add Website". The Websites card should have a "View More" that goes to the Websites tab.

### HTTPS Status Card
Beginner-friendly. When a domain is first connected, show progression DNS Ready -> SSL Issuing -> HTTPS Verified. Once verified, show the verified status alongside other website/hosting details instead of continuing to show the setup process.

### Storage Breakdown
Card showing where the customer's storage is being used.

### Recent Activity
Card showing relevant activity across the hosting plan.

### Subscription
Card showing: renewal price, add-ons currently attached to the plan, auto-renew status, Manage Plan, Upgrade Plan. Keep compact.

## WEBSITES
Each website attached to the hosting plan needs to be treated as its own segregated website. The hosting plan controls the overall limits, not individual websites (e.g. total number of websites, total databases, total storage, total bandwidth are all limited by the plan). Individual websites should therefore have their own isolated environment within the plan. Each website should have its own dashboard where the customer can manage: domains/subdomains, files, database, installed applications. Each website should be able to have either a free Nxeon subdomain (e.g. example.sites.nxeon.cloud) or a custom domain. Each website should have its own filesystem and database.

## FILES
Use the EXACT SAME file-management system already used in the VPS Dashboard and Game Server Dashboard. Do not create a completely different file manager. Retain: file browser, folder navigation, upload system, upload queue, real upload progress, search, sorting, file actions.

## DATABASES
We currently have our proprietary simplified version of phpMyAdmin called Nxeon DB Studio. I want to improve DB Studio. Review the existing DB Studio implementation and compare its functionality feature-for-feature against established database management tools (phpMyAdmin, MongoDB management tools, PostgreSQL management tools). Identify where DB Studio is currently falling short and what functionality needs to be added. DO NOT BLINDLY ADD FEATURES — identify the gaps first so the user can decide what should actually be implemented. (This section is a research + written report deliverable, not a build-everything-you-find deliverable — see "YOUR DELIVERABLE" below.)

## SETTINGS
Should contain, organized/separated rather than one cluttered page: Upgrade Plan, PHP Version (change it), Storage (increase allocation), Cancel Hosting.

## FTP / ACCESS
Need a clear, logical place for FTP access details — current implementation is poorly organized and makes credentials hard to find. If multiple FTP logins are not currently supported, add support for them. Customers should be able to create multiple FTP credentials. Each FTP credential should support permissions/access restrictions so a customer can give someone access to only specific folders rather than the whole hosting plan (e.g. FTP User A -> /website1/, FTP User B -> /website2/uploads/). The customer should control which folders each FTP account can access.

## IMPORTANT CLEANUP
The existing dashboard shows contradictory/redundant things simultaneously — e.g. SFTP credentials, WordPress credentials, "Your account is ready", "Install WordPress", AND "WordPress installation complete" all shown at once even when WordPress is already installed. Clean this up completely: only show information/actions relevant to the CURRENT state of the customer's hosting plan.

## FINAL DESIGN DIRECTION
Use the VPS Dashboard as the primary visual reference. Should feel like the exact same product ecosystem, optimized around websites/shared hosting rather than VPS management. Prioritize: clean hierarchy, strong visual organization, premium dark UI, blue/purple Nxeon accents, subtle gradients/glows, interactive cards, clear usage indicators, minimal redundancy, easy navigation, strong visual distinction between the hosting PLAN and individual WEBSITES.
---

FACTS TO ORIENT YOU (verified before dispatching you, but confirm anything load-bearing yourself):
- The CURRENT shared-hosting UI has never been touched by the Nexion redesign — it's still the original pre-redesign design. Entry points: app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx (list) and app/dashboard/hosting/[id]/page.tsx (one hosting account), rendering components/customer/HostingClient.tsx and components/customer/hosting/*.tsx (HostingTabs.tsx, WebsitesPanel.tsx, DatabasesPanel.tsx, DbManager.tsx — THIS is "Nxeon DB Studio", FileManager.tsx, Backups.tsx, CronPanel.tsx, EmailTab.tsx, SubdomainsPanel.tsx, AddonDomainsPanel.tsx, AppInstaller.tsx, AppCredentials.tsx, PhpSwitcher.tsx, PlanUpgrade.tsx, OverviewIcons.tsx, shared.tsx). Read all of these to understand the REAL current data model and REAL current capabilities before designing the replacement — the redundant/contradictory states the user describes (SFTP + WordPress creds + "ready" + "install" + "installed" all at once) are almost certainly really there; find and fix the actual state logic, don't just hide things cosmetically.
- The current FTP/SFTP credential UI is components/customer/SftpAccess.tsx — read it and its backing server actions/schema to find out whether multiple credentials and per-folder permission scoping already exist at the data layer. If not, this is real backend work (new Prisma model/fields + server actions), not just UI — do it properly, following whatever pattern lib/actions-server.ts or lib/actions-disk.ts use for a real, job-backed or directly-applied server-side change. Never render a UI that pretends multiple scoped FTP users exist if the backend can't actually enforce the scoping.
- The VPS dashboard's visual language — your reference for EVERYTHING visual — lives in components/customer/vpspanel/v2/ (kit.tsx has the reusable primitives: `Panel`, `StatusPill`, `Metric`, `Segmented`, `CopyChip`; `ui.tsx` has `SubNav`/`Card`; the whole panel uses `card card-glass` with a `--tone` CSS custom property throughout — read VpsPanelShell.tsx and VpsOverviewPanel.tsx as your primary references for hero + tab-shell shape). This session ALSO just fully rebuilt the VPS "Resources" tab (VpsResourcesPanel.tsx, VpsPlanChart.tsx, VpsStorageMeter.tsx, VpsAddonsCard.tsx, VpsUpgradeCart.tsx) — that is a second, very relevant reference for things like your Settings tab's "Upgrade Plan"/storage-increase controls and your Websites-grid-card layout ambitions, since it already solved "plan comparison chart", "interactive storage slider reusing a real asset", and "sticky cart + payment sheet" for the VPS case — reuse/adapt these patterns rather than reinventing them for hosting.
- File management: components/customer/files/UploadQueue.tsx and whatever renders alongside it (grep for its usage in the VPS/game file-browser tabs) is the ACTUAL shared file manager the user wants you to reuse for hosting's Files tab and each website's own file view — do not build a new one.
- Theme: this whole session has been building a light theme (toggle via `data-theme="light"` on `<html>`, tokens as `--color-*` CSS custom properties in app/globals.css) on top of what was previously dark-only. Build your NEW hosting v2 UI theme-safe from day one — use the existing tokens (`text-tx`, `text-tx-dim`, `text-tx-faint`, `border-rim-hi`, `bg-well`, `bg-surface`, `.card`/`.card-glass`) throughout, exactly like the VPS v2 panel does, rather than hardcoding literal colors that would need retrofitting later. Use `.nx-dark-island` (also in app/globals.css) only for something that must always render dark regardless of theme (e.g. a photographic website-preview thumbnail's own caption strip, mirroring how components/nx/WhatsNewView.tsx's GameCoverTile caption was just fixed this session — grep `git log -p -1 --follow components/nx/WhatsNewView.tsx` or just `git diff HEAD~3 -- components/nx/WhatsNewView.tsx` if that helps you see the exact pattern). Verify your new UI in BOTH themes before finishing, the same screenshot-based way used throughout this session (scripts/ directory, Playwright, `localStorage.setItem('nx-theme','light')` before navigating).
- Data model: check prisma/schema.prisma for the real HostingAccount/Website/Domain-adjacent models (grep for "model Hosting" and "model.*Website" and "model.*Subdomain") to see what "each website has its own isolated filesystem and database" would actually require at the schema level, and whether it's already modeled that way or needs real schema changes (`npm run db:push` after editing prisma/schema.prisma — there are no migration files in this repo, remember the two node-2/primary databases are separate).

FABRICATION GUARDRAILS — read carefully, this is the part most likely to go wrong:
1. **Auto-scraped website screenshots**: investigate whether any screenshot-capture pipeline already exists anywhere in this codebase (grep for "screenshot", "puppeteer", check package.json — Playwright is already a project dependency used for this session's own testing, so a real server-side "launch headless chromium, navigate to the site, screenshot it, store the image" action is genuinely buildable, not fantasy). If you build it, make it REAL (an actual server action/job that actually navigates to the domain and captures a real image, with a real pending/failed state while it hasn't run yet) — never fake a screenshot image or hardcode a stock photo pretending to be "the customer's site". If a real pipeline is too large to fully wire end-to-end (e.g. into a job queue) in this pass, it is fine to ship the placeholder + custom-upload paths as fully real and working, with the auto-scrape slot clearly in a "not yet captured" state rather than showing something fake.
2. **Per-website isolation**: only claim/imply "isolated filesystem and database" in the UI to the extent the backend genuinely provides it after your changes. If you scope this pass to the UI/IA layer over the EXISTING (possibly shared/flatter) backend model, say so honestly in your report rather than letting the UI imply stronger isolation than is real.
3. **DB Studio**: this section is explicitly RESEARCH FIRST. Read components/customer/hosting/DbManager.tsx fully, actually use it live (log in, open a real hosting account's DB Studio, try creating a table, running a query, editing a row, exporting, managing users/permissions if that's a thing it does) and compare feature-for-feature against what phpMyAdmin/a Postgres GUI/a Mongo GUI offer. Produce a clear written gap list in your final report (what exists, what's missing, roughly how hard each gap would be) — implement only small, obviously-safe, high-value gaps if you have time left after everything else, but the primary deliverable for this section is the ANALYSIS, not a feature-complete phpMyAdmin clone.
4. **FTP folder-scoped permissions**: real backend enforcement or don't claim it works — see above.

WORKFLOW: this is a large, multi-file effort — budget your time accordingly and go deep rather than shallow. Read the existing hosting components and the VPS v2 reference components FULLY before writing any code. Build the new hosting v2 surface under components/customer/hosting/v2/ (mirroring the vpspanel/v2 naming convention), wire it in from app/dashboard/hosting/[id]/page.tsx, and remove/retire the old cluttered UI paths you're replacing (don't leave two competing dashboards live). Iterate with `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit`, rebuild with `./rebuild.sh` per the concurrency guidance above, and do real logged-in Playwright screenshot passes in both themes as you go — this whole task exists because the current dashboard looks and works badly, so seeing it rendered matters a lot here.

Write a thorough final report: what you built (mapped to each section of the user's spec above), what real backend capability each piece maps to, the full DB Studio gap analysis, and any place you scoped down from the literal spec (and why) so the user can decide whether to invest further.

content.content: 1 # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork 2 3 **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with 4 a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The 5 code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but 6 `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. 7 8 Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the 9 direction and the history of what has been built. 10 11 --- 12 13 ## Where you are, and what that changes 14 15 This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is 16 meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: 17 18 ```bash 19 hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. 20 ``` 21 22 **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: 23 24 ```bash 25 npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build 26 ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. 27 ``` 28 29 **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also 30 runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, 31 terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A 32 `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, 33 then: 34 35 ```bash 36 scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 37 ``` 38 39 It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) 40 and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. 41 42 **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on 43 node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not 44 deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's 45 commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. 46 47 ## The tree 48 49 | | | 50 |---|---| 51 | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | 52 | Branch | `design/v2` | 53 | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | 54 | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | 55 | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | 56 | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | 57 | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | 58 59 `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and 60 it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` 61 builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. 62 63 Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node 64 and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing 65 to the other. 66 67 ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here 68 69 node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because 70 three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept 71 attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the 72 production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox 73 seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. 74 75 Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two 76 levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: 77 78 ```bash 79 scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title 80 scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments 81 scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ 82 scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD 83 scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else 84 ``` 85 86 **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production 87 database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod 88 DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, 89 not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never 90 restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, 91 **stop and ask the owner first.** 92 93 ## Rules that are not negotiable 94 95 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs 96 or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real 97 upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had 98 hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not 99 reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a 100 `0` that reads as a real measurement. 101 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its 102 `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 103 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` 104 restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 105 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real 106 `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 107 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and 108 before spending on any paid third-party tool. 109 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 110 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 111 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. 112 113 ## Verification discipline 114 115 A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a 116 login-and-capture script: 117 118 ```bash 119 node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings 120 # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS 121 ``` 122 123 Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read 124 the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar 125 and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. 126 127 ## Things that have already cost hours here 128 129 - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. 130 - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to 131 a file and use `git commit -F`. 132 - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, 133 which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. 134 - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page 135 content needs `relative z-[1]`. 136 - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` 137 children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. 138 - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's 139 bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let 140 the layout place things. 141 - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. 142 - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check 143 `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. 144 - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress 145 needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. 146 - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted 147 `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each 148 took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route 149 a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` 150 must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. 151 152 ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) 153 154 - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox 155 mutation endpoints directly. 156 - One in-flight job per server. 157 - Wallet amounts are integer cents. 158 - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. 159 - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a 160 charting library. 161 162 ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here 163 164 The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at 165 `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY 166 node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: 167 168 - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. 169 This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. 170 - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. 171 - **Do not** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`. 172 - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: 173 `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually. 174

1	# Nexion v2 — direction, what exists, what is open
2	
3	Companion to `CLAUDE.md`. That file is how to operate this tree; this one is what
4	we are building and why, so a session starting cold can carry on without
5	re-deriving it.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. What Nexion is
10	
11	A from-scratch visual language for the Nxeon customer portal, built over the
12	real backend rather than as a mockup. The point is not a reskin: pages get
13	**structurally rebuilt** around what the customer is actually trying to do, and
14	the real data is wired through as we go.
15	
16	The owner's direction, stated repeatedly and worth taking literally:
17	
18	- **"This is really generic and bad."** Templated layouts get rejected. Work
19	  from the supplied concept, and improvise where the concept is thin — do not
20	  produce the safe default.
21	- **"Do not simply modify the existing dashboard."** Rebuild, don't patch.
22	- **Concepts are on the admin board**, which lives on node-1. Card attachments
23	  are rows in prod Postgres (`CardAttachment` ⋈ `Card`) with files on disk at
24	  `/opt/nxeon/board-uploads/board/<cardId>/<storedName>`. From node-2, reach them
25	  with `scripts/node1.sh cards|board|pull` — see CLAUDE.md, and note that the
26	  same grant reaches live production, so it is read-only. Compare against the
27	  concepts *during* the build, not only at the end.
28	- **The owner's own premium art is in `board-uploads`** — find it by alpha scan
29	  rather than scraping stock imagery.
30	
31	### Design tokens
32	
33	CSS custom properties: `--color-well`, `--color-rim-soft`, `--color-rim-hi`,
34	`--color-tx-dim`, `--color-tx-faint`.
35	Classes: `.card`, `.nx-cta`, `.btn-deploy` (+ `.dep-arrow`), `.grad-text`,
36	`.nx-breathe`, `.section-label`, `.badge` / `.badge-amber`, `.num`, `.mono`.
37	Brand ramp: `#3fbcd8 → #4f7cff → #d623e1` (from the logo; magenta is a
38	placeholder until the exact hex arrives).
39	
40	Icons: `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts`, rendered by `components/nx/Icon.tsx`. **Check a
41	name exists before using it** — there is no `alert`/`info`/`check`; they are
42	`warntriangle` / `warncircle` / `checkcircle`.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## 2. The honesty rule, in practice
47	
48	This is the single most load-bearing convention in the tree, and the one most
49	easily undone by a well-meaning change.
50	
51	The storefront this replaced drew a star rating, an install count, a version
52	history and two customer reviews for every mod — **all computed from a hash of
53	the mod's slug**, because the table had no such columns. "4.7 stars · 84k
54	installs" read as fact. The reviews had invented authors saying invented things.
55	All of it was deleted.
56	
57	What replaced it is the same information where it is *real*, and silence where
58	it is not. Concretely, things this tree deliberately does **not** show:
59	
60	- No storage ceiling on backups (sizes are summed; the quota does not exist).
61	- No one-click world restore (no action relocates a path).
62	- No move/copy in the file manager (same reason).
63	- No ETA or bytes-transferred on a migration.
64	- No disk-usage bar in the destination picker.
65	- No live player count for a game with no public query protocol — the card says
66	  the game has none, rather than rendering `0`.
67	- No compatibility verdict for a mod whose source publishes no version list.
68	
69	When you are tempted to fill a gap, fill it with the *reason* the gap exists.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## 3. Shared helpers — use them, don't re-derive
74	
75	Several outages here came from the same formula existing twice. These exist so
76	that cannot happen again:
77	
78	| Module | Answers |
79	|---|---|
80	| `lib/nx/connect-address.ts` | The address a customer can actually reach a server on. **Never** `Server.ipAddress` — that is the internal 10.20.x.x NAT address. |
81	| `lib/nx/plan-specs.ts` | `gamePlanSpecs()` / `specLine()` — spec strings, with the leading game name stripped. |
82	| `lib/mod-load.ts` | "Am I running too many mods?" — and the measured/judgement split. |
83	| `lib/mod-install-support.ts` | Whether a one-click install can possibly work. Imported by `worker/game-mods.ts` so UI and worker cannot disagree. |
84	| `lib/server-query.ts` | Live player counts over the public game-query protocols. |
85	| `lib/game-resize.ts` | Game-tier upgrade pricing. Prices against `gamePlan.priceCents`, **not** `plan.priceCents`. |
86	
87	Pricing traps worth knowing: renewal price is `renewalCharge`, not
88	`plan.priceCents` (a $4.99 game server rides a $8.99 base plan and was being
89	advertised at the wrong one). Game plans are priced for their *own* term, so a
90	monthly rate is `priceCents / termMonths`.
91	
92	---
93	
94	## 4. What has been built
95	
96	### Game server dashboard — `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/`
97	Complete redesign, not a modification. Sticky game-specific hero + tab rail that
98	travel together, so identity, vitals and power controls are reachable from every
99	tab. Ten tabs consolidated from thirteen: Overview, Console, Files, Mods &
100	Plugins, Backups, Players, Schedules, Build with AI, Settings, Activity.
101	
102	- `GameHero.tsx` — full-bleed key art, **centred**, feathered at both edges
103	  (symmetric horizontal mask + vertical fade + floor gradient). Real Proxmox RRD
104	  sparklines; a server with no history draws a flat baseline and says so. An
105	  earlier version seeded them with a synthetic sine wave — that is a drawing of
106	  data that does not exist.
107	- `GamePanelShell.tsx` — tabs in the URL via `pushState` + `popstate` (the old
108	  shell used `replaceState`, so Back skipped the whole panel). `ALIASES` maps
109	  retired tab keys that worker notifications still deep-link to. `LEGACY_CARDS`
110	  re-skins the shared `.card` class only where Players/Schedules/CommandLibrary
111	  mount, instead of changing it app-wide.
112	- `GameSettingsShell.tsx` — six sections with "Upgrade your server resources"
113	  first and the destructive ones fenced at the end.
114	- `TierUpgrade.tsx` + `lib/game-resize.ts` — self-service upgrades, replacing
115	  "our team moves you across manually". **Upgrades only**; a downgrade refunds,
116	  and that direction is not self-service until someone has sat with the maths.
117	- `components/customer/files/` — three-pane browser with lazy tree nodes and an
118	  XHR upload progress queue.
119	
120	### Mods & Plugins — real catalogue
121	`scripts/verify-gamemods.ts` reads every entry from its own upstream and imports
122	the most-downloaded server-side projects per family.
123	
124	Sources and what each can answer: **modrinth** (versions, loaders, downloads,
125	size, deps, side) · **spigotmc/spiget** (downloads, size, tested versions) ·
126	**thunderstore** (downloads, size, deps) · **umod** (downloads; size by HEAD, no
127	version list) · **github** (release tag, asset size/downloads) · **factorio**
128	(versions, downloads, deps; no size) · **ficsit** (version, downloads, size) ·
129	**nexus** (nothing — needs an API key, so those entries stay unverified and are
130	never marked dead).
131	
132	Two rules that matter: a **404 retires an entry, a timeout does not** (the first
133	version conflated them and marked ten live Rust plugins dead when uMod briefly
134	stopped answering); and a source that cannot answer for a field **must not erase
135	it**.
136	
137	`ModsPanel.tsx` shows an aggregate load banner, per-mod heavy warnings from the
138	real file size, and a compatibility verdict only where the source publishes a
139	version list. Heavy or mismatched installs confirm first.
140	
141	**Verified 2026-09-11:** `ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS=1` in prod's `.env` (checked via
142	`scripts/node1.sh sh`, read-only). The real path is live, not dark — this
143	catalogue and its install support matter to real customers today.
144	
145	### Matrix — `components/nx/MatrixPanel.tsx`
146	The multi-console AI build workspace. It rendered **nothing** until recently:
147	`MatrixProvider` is mounted in `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (the live portal's
148	shell) and the Nexion shell never mounted it. Now an ordinary block inside
149	`<main>`, mounted at shell level so consoles and their websockets survive
150	navigation, with `MatrixRain.tsx` as the backdrop (brand ramp, ~22fps, parks when
151	hidden or off-screen, stops dead under `prefers-reduced-motion`).
152	
153	### Server Directory — `/dashboard/directory`
154	In-portal, under Tools. Region, connect address, game key art, search and
155	filters. `lib/server-query.ts` reads live player counts over Minecraft's Server
156	List Ping, Bedrock's RakNet ping, and Valve's A2S_INFO (including the post-2020
157	challenge). Opt-in is `GamePublicListing`, mounted in the game panel's Network
158	settings — it and `Server.publicListing` both already existed with nothing
159	rendering them.
160	
161	### Others
162	- **My Services** (`lib/nx/services.ts`, `components/customer/services/`) — one
163	  consolidated estate view with preview images; replaced three per-product rails.
164	- **Free Minecraft** (`components/customer/freemc/`) — rebuilt on the paid
165	  panel's hero + rail, minus the vitals a shared-node container cannot report.
166	- **Settings** (`components/nx/SettingsView.tsx`) — full rewrite; Integrations
167	  (Cloudflare / Anthropic / Discord) restored.
168	- **Migration** (`components/customer/migrate/`) — stages driven by **stage
169	  name**, not percent; the engine's percentages are non-monotonic.
170	- **Build with Claude Code** (`components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx`)
171	  — four tabs instead of a 5,400px scroll; all emoji replaced with the portal's
172	  own icon set.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. Open — decisions and gaps
177	
178	### Needs an owner decision
179	- **`deepestPromoPercent()` → 100% proration fallback.** When
180	  `Server.termPromoPercent` is null, `resolveTermPromoPercent` falls back to the
181	  deepest promo, which is now `FIRST_MONTH_FREE` at 100% — so an upgrade's whole
182	  price delta discounts away to £0. Live rows are backfilled so it is unreachable
183	  today (one null row: `kodely-app`, isFree, no expiry). The game path has a
184	  refusal guard. **Not fixed at source, because that reprices real customers.**
185	- **A Steam Web API key** would unlock mod catalogues for roughly twenty more
186	  games (ARK, Conan, Garry's Mod, Project Zomboid, Unturned, Terraria, The
187	  Forest, 7 Days to Die…). It is free but registers against the owner's Steam
188	  account and domain, so it is theirs to create, not ours.
189	
190	### Known gaps, flagged and not closed
191	- **Mod catalogue covers 12 of 42 sold families.** The rest are Steam Workshop
192	  games (needs the key above) or genuinely have no mod platform (Bedrock,
193	  Enshrouded, Icarus, Necesse, Eco, Soulmask, Abiotic Factor, Dragonwilds).
194	- **One-click install works for 3 families** (minecraft, rust, valheim) and 4 of
195	  9 sources. `lib/mod-install-support.ts` makes the UI honest about it; wiring
196	  more means adding a directory to `worker/game-mods.ts`'s `modDirShell` **and**
197	  the slug to `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES` — both, or it breaks again.
198	- **Game settings apply for 4 of 43 families; RCON for 3 of 43.** The tier-change
199	  quote says so before the money moves.
200	- My Services follow-ups never built: auto-renew visibility, suspension recovery
201	  path, spend / next-renewal summary strip.
202	- ~~The free-Minecraft game-mode selector still uses emoji~~ — checked
203	  2026-09-11: `GameModeSelector.tsx` already renders hand-drawn per-mode SVG
204	  glyphs, deliberately without hero imagery (see its own file doc). Stale
205	  claim, nothing to fix.
206	- ~~The create form has a large empty right column~~ — fixed 2026-09-11: the
207	  `/dashboard/games` tab now renders a live preview panel next to the form
208	  (`FreeMinecraftPanel.tsx`'s `showPreview`) showing the selected game type's
209	  real hero art, the typed subdomain, and the selected mode. The
210	  `/dashboard/services` claim panel already filled its width with its own
211	  pitch column and is unchanged.
212	- Older open task chips: two dead free-Minecraft signup links
213	  (`task_510e81cc`), an aurora-layer audit, a domains hydration error.
214	
215	### Sandbox demo data
216	Four public listings were seeded on node-2 so the directory is not empty — three
217	paid (`survival-smp`, `wasteland`, `creative-flats`) and one free (`stonefall`,
218	`fmc_demo_0001`). They are sandbox rows, safe to delete.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## 6. Working agreement
223	
224	- Deploy and screenshot every change; read the screenshot back.
225	- Extract a shared helper rather than copying a formula.
226	- Verify a claim against the database or a live API before asserting it — doing
227	  that has caught several of this session's own wrong claims, including a
228	  "19 games" figure that came from sandbox seed data when production sells 42.
229	- When a request is ambiguous, do the routine judgement call and say which
230	  reading you took.

model TelemetryEvent {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  // One of these two identifies the source; VPS/GAME events set serverId,
  // HOSTING/MAIL events (centralized shippers) set nodeId + nodeKind instead.
  serverId  String?
  server    Server?  @relation(fields: [serverId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  nodeId    String? // HostingNode.id for HOSTING; a fixed constant for MAIL (see lib/telemetry.ts)
  nodeKind  String // VPS | GAME | HOSTING | MAIL
  type      String // SSH_LOGIN | SSH_LOGOUT | SSH_FAILED | VISITOR | MAIL_AUTH
  ts        DateTime @default(now()) // event time as reported by the shipper
  ip        String?
  user      String?
  path      String? // VISITOR request path
  site      String? // which vhost/customer site, on a centralized HOSTING shipper
  status    String?
  meta      String?
  label     String? // hostname/display label the shipper reported, for the UI
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) // ingest time — what the prune sweep keys off

  @@index([createdAt])
  @@index([serverId, createdAt])
  @@index([nodeKind, createdAt])
}

model Improvement {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  batchId      String? // groups one nightly scan
  category     String // bug | feature | error | enhancement | security | performance
  severity     String   @default("medium") // low | medium | high | critical
  title        String
  summary      String // one-to-two sentence concise description (owner reads this)
  detail       String? // longer optional detail, collapsed by default
  source       String? // nightly-scan | feedback | error-log | bug-report | audit
  effort       String? // S | M | L
  filesHint    String? // suggested files/areas to change
  status       String   @default("PROPOSED") // PROPOSED | APPROVED | DECLINED | IN_PROGRESS | DONE
  resolvedNote String?
  ownerNote    String? // owner's instructions for how to handle this item
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  @@index([status])
  @@index([batchId])
}

// ============================================================================
// Website Builder (Wix-style) — additive only. A Site is edited in-browser and
// PUBLISHES INTO an existing Website row (reusing nginx/SSL/domain machinery);
// websiteId is a scalar FK on purpose so this never touches the Website model.
// ============================================================================
model Site {
  id          String        @id @default(cuid())
  userId      String
  name        String
  slug        String // the *.nxeon subdomain label; globally unique
  websiteId   String? // the Website row it publishes into once live
  status      String        @default("DRAFT") // DRAFT | PUBLISHING | PUBLISHED | FAILED
  templateKey String? // starter template it began from
  publishedAt DateTime?
  error       String?
  createdAt   DateTime      @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime      @updatedAt

## 4. Broken, misleading, or unsupportable-claim findings

These are the CLAUDE.md rule-1 adjacent items. Ordered by severity.

**B1 — Structure tab shows the column COMMENT under a "Collation" header.** `DbManager.tsx:973` headers are `["Column","Type","Null","Key","Default","Extra","Collation",""]`; the 7th `<td>` at `:989` renders `{c.comment}`. `fetchStructure` (`actions-hosting-db.ts:414-422`) never reads `r[2]`, which is where `SHOW FULL COLUMNS` puts Collation. So the column is always mislabelled, and for the common case (no comments) it renders `·` — a customer reads that as "this column has no collation". Straight mislabelling of data. **S.**

**B2 — Exports are silently truncated at 1000 rows.** `dumpSelectSql` (`hosting-db.ts:411`) is `SELECT * FROM t LIMIT 1000`, and the transport caps at 1000 rows / 2 MiB regardless. `dbmgrExportTable` *returns* `truncated`, but `exportAs` in `DbManager.tsx:534-540` **ignores it** and just downloads. The SQL dump buries `-- rows: 1000 (truncated at 1000)` in a header comment; **the CSV has no marker at all**. A customer with a 40k-row `wp_posts` downloads a file they believe is their table and it is 2.5% of it. This is the single most damaging item in the file: it produces a plausible-looking artifact that is wrong. **S to warn, M to fix properly.**

**B3 — `SET` / transactions / temp tables silently no-op during Import.** `dbmgrImportSql` (`:801`) loops `await runScopedSql(...)` per statement, and `runScopedSql` opens a **brand-new SSH tunnel and MySQL session every call**. Session state does not survive between statements. Consequences: `SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0;` does nothing; `START TRANSACTION` / `COMMIT` do nothing; `SET NAMES`, `SET @var`, temp tables do nothing. **Studio's own SQL export emits `SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0;` as line 1** (`actions-hosting-db.ts:611`) — so DB Studio produces a dump that DB Studio's own importer cannot faithfully re-import once FKs are involved. Every statement reports `ok: true` while the intended semantics are lost. **M.**

**B4 — Binary data is silently corrupted.** `cellToString` (`hosting-db.ts:262`) does `Buffer.toString("utf8")` on every BLOB/BINARY value. That value is then (a) rendered, (b) used as the `WHERE` identity for an inline edit or delete, and (c) written into the SQL dump via `dumpValueLiteral` → `sqlEscape(string)`. A round-trip through export/import mangles binary columns, and an inline edit of any row in a table with a BLOB PK/identity column will fail to match or write back mojibake. No warning anywhere. **M.**

**B5 — Row counts in the sidebar are presented as facts.** `dbmgrTableCounts` reads `information_schema.TABLES.TABLE_ROWS`, which for InnoDB is a sampled estimate routinely off by tens of percent. The Overview stat tile says "Rows (approx)" and the prose says "approximate", but **the sidebar badge (`DbManager.tsx:246`) and the Overview table's "Rows" column header (`:365`) present it bare**. Cheap fix: title attribute / "≈" prefix. **S.**

**B6 — A failed structure fetch is reported as "no primary key".** `TableBrowser`'s structure load (`:424-428`) swallows errors (`if (!cancelled && r.structure)`). On failure: Insert row stays disabled with no explanation and the grid prints *"Inline editing needs a primary key — use the row editor instead"* (`:904`) — a wrong diagnosis of a transport failure. **S.**

**B7 — The destructive-SQL confirm is bypassable and noisy.** `DESTRUCTIVE_RE` (`:1321`) is anchored `^\s*`, so `-- backup first\nDROP TABLE users;` runs with no confirmation. It also fires on `create` and `update`, training users to click through. **S.**

**B8 — Sandbox mode returns invented data through the real UI.** `SANDBOX_TABLES = ["customers","orders","products"]`, `sandboxResult()` returning Ada Lovelace / Grace Hopper rows, `dbmgrTableCounts` returning `[42, 17, 88]`, `dbmgrDatabaseOverview` returning hardcoded byte sizes (`actions-hosting-db.ts:187-204, 462, 646-650`). It is clearly gated on `SANDBOX` and never reaches production, but it is exactly the shape rule 1 warns about: the UI renders a confident number with no indication it is fabricated. If this tree is ever demoed, someone will screenshot "88 products". A "sandbox — demo data" banner in the Studio header would close it. **S.**

**B9 — Views are unreachable from the UI but reachable by the backend.** The tree and Overview filter to `BASE TABLE`; the membership check uses `SHOW TABLES`, which *includes* views. So a customer whose app uses views sees an empty/incomplete table list and has no hint the objects exist. **S.**

**B10 — Performance: every UI action costs multiple SSH handshakes.** There is no connection pooling or caching; `runScopedSql` connects and disconnects per statement. Measured by reading the call graphs:
- Opening a table in Browse = `SHOW TABLES` + `SHOW FULL COLUMNS` + the `SELECT` + the `COUNT` (`dbmgrBrowseTable`) **plus** `dbmgrTableStructure`'s `SHOW TABLES` + `SHOW FULL COLUMNS` + `SHOW INDEX` = **7 SSH+MySQL connections**.
- Switching to Structure adds 4 more (3 + `SHOW CREATE TABLE` via `dbmgrRunSql`).
- `dbmgrInsertRow`/`UpdateRow`/`DeleteRow` each re-run the full membership + structure preamble = **4 connections per row**. The bulk delete in `DbManager.tsx:508-523` loops one row at a time → **deleting 50 selected rows = ~200 sequential SSH connections.**
- A 200-statement import = 200 SSH connections.

With `DB_MGR_MAX_CONNECTIONS = 5` and a 20 s connect timeout, this is the reason DB Studio will feel slow next to phpMyAdmin, which holds one connection for a whole page. **Not broken, but it is the thing that will make customers say "this is worse than phpMyAdmin".**

**B11 — There is no way to delete a hosting database, or get your data out.** No `deleteHostingDatabase` action exists anywhere (`HostingDatabaseStatus.DELETING` at `schema.prisma:1806` is never set for this model). And `Backups.tsx` offers only "Back up now" / "Restore" — **no download**; `taskBackup` (`worker/hosting.ts:1382`) mysqldumps into a root-only dir on the node. Combined with B2, **a shared-hosting customer has no supported way to obtain a complete copy of their own database.** That is a retention and arguably a GDPR-portability problem, not just a feature gap.

| 3 | **Label estimated row counts** (B5) + fix the "needs a primary key" misdiagnosis (B6) + tighten `DESTRUCTIVE_RE` (B7) | Honesty + one confusing dead-end | **S** each |
| 4 | **Export the SQL tab's results** (CSV/SQL button on `ResultGrid`) | phpMyAdmin's single most-used workflow: query, then take the answer to a spreadsheet. `toCsv` already exists; it's a button over data already on the client | **S** |
| 5 | **List views** — add `TABLE_TYPE='VIEW'` to `tableCountsSql`/`overviewSql`, render with a distinct icon, browse read-only (the backend already permits it) | Customers with views currently see a lying table list | **S** |
| 6 | **Bulk row delete in one statement** — `DELETE … WHERE (pk) IN (…)` instead of an N-round-trip loop | 200 SSH connections → 4 for a 50-row delete | **S** |
| 7 | **Sandbox "demo data" banner** (B8) | rule 1 hygiene | **S** |

### Tier 2 — a new action each, clearly worth it

| # | Gap | Why it matters | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | **Create table form** (`dbmgrCreateTable`) — name, columns (type/null/default/AI/PK), engine/collation | You currently cannot create a table without hand-writing DDL. This is the #1 thing a beginner opens phpMyAdmin to do, and DB Studio's target user is a shared-hosting beginner | **M** |
| 9 | **Full-database export** (B11) — `dbmgrExportDatabase`, all tables, streamed | Migration-out, "give me a backup before I upgrade", GDPR. Today there is no path at all | **M** (see #13 for the streaming part) |
| 10 | **Modify column** (`dbmgrModifyColumn` → `ALTER TABLE … MODIFY/CHANGE`) — rename, retype, null/not-null, default | Only ADD and DROP exist; changing a column today means drop+re-add, which destroys the data. This is a foot-gun, not just a gap | **M** |
| 11 | **Richer Add Column / Add Index** — DEFAULT, AUTO_INCREMENT, UNSIGNED, ENUM/SET, `AFTER <col>`, comment; PRIMARY/FULLTEXT index kinds. `normalizeColumnType` (`hosting-db.ts:500`) currently rejects all of these | The add-column form can't express most real schemas | **M** |
| 12 | **Drop a database** + a plan-cap-aware confirm | Customers can create up to `maxDatabases` and then are stuck forever | **M** |
| 13 | **Streaming download route for exports** — an `app/api/hosting/db/export/route.ts` alongside the existing `app/api/hosting/files/route.ts`, so a dump isn't a string in an RSC payload | Precondition for #9 and for lifting the 1000-row cap; the file-manager route is the template | **M** |
| 14 | **phpMyAdmin-style Search tab** — per-column operator (`=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `LIKE`, `IS NULL`, `BETWEEN`) with AND/OR. Today filters are LIKE-contains, AND-only | The non-SQL user's only query tool | **M** |
| 15 | **Binary column handling** (B4) — detect BLOB/BINARY from the structure, render `[BLOB 12.3 KB]` instead of mojibake, make it read-only inline, hex-literal it in dumps | Prevents silent corruption | **M** |
| 16 | **EXPLAIN button** on the SQL tab | Shared hosting kills slow queries; this is how a customer self-diagnoses. One extra `runScopedSql` behind a toggle | **S–M** |

### Tier 3 — real backend work, but strategically important

| # | Gap | Why it matters | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | **Connection reuse / session-scoped transport** — hold one SSH tunnel + MySQL session for the duration of a multi-statement operation, and cache `SHOW TABLES`/columns per request (B3, B10) | Fixes the broken `SET`/transaction semantics in Import *and* the 7-connections-per-click latency at the same time. This is the highest-leverage backend change on the list | **L** |
| 18 | **Real import pipeline** — chunked/resumable upload (the files API already does uploads), `.sql.gz`, no 512 KB / 200-statement cap, progress, optional "continue on error" | Today the migration-in story is: your WordPress dump is 8 MB, so you cannot use this product. This is the single biggest reason a customer leaves for a host with phpMyAdmin. Depends on #17 and #13 | **L** |
| 19 | **Foreign keys** — a Relations panel (read from `information_schema.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE`), FK create/drop, and click-through navigation from a FK cell to the parent row (TablePlus/pgAdmin convention, very learnable) | Invisible today except inside `SHOW CREATE TABLE` | **L** (read-only view alone is **M**) |
| 20 | **Database users & grants** — additional users per database, per-user privilege selection | phpMyAdmin's Users tab. Real demand from customers running an app + a read-only reporting user. Needs worker/root involvement since `_mgr` cannot `CREATE USER` | **L** |
| 21 | **Views / triggers / routines / events** — list, view definition, create | Full parity item; low demand on shared hosting | **L** |
| 22 | **Backup download** (`Backups.tsx`) | Complements #9; the tarball already exists on the node and is root-owned. Needs a signed streaming route | **M–L** |

### Things phpMyAdmin has that I'd deliberately *not* build
Designer/ER canvas, transformation plugins, multi-server switching, per-user pmadb config storage, the Charts tab. Nothing in this codebase suggests demand, and Studio's value is being simpler.

### Conventions worth stealing from elsewhere
- **TablePlus/pgAdmin**: FK click-through (#19) and a "changes staged, commit/discard" edit buffer rather than DB Studio's write-on-blur inline edit — currently a fat-finger writes immediately with no undo.
- **Compass**: nothing applicable; there is no Mongo in the platform.
- **pgAdmin**: the query-plan visualiser is the good version of #16 if it's ever worth more than a text `EXPLAIN`.

## 6. Verification note — I could not click through the live sandbox

I tried. Two blockers, both verified, neither worked around:

"use client";

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import Link from "next/link";
import { Icon, Plate } from "./Icon";
import { SvcIcon } from "./SvcIcon";

/* The provisioning screen, in the Nexion language.
 *
 * The design sandbox animated this on a TIMER — five stages with hardcoded
 * durations that marched to 100% whether or not anything was happening. That
 * does not survive the port. The platform already records genuine progress:
 * the worker writes a short human label between real, observable command groups
 * (lib/provisioning-step.ts) and returns null when there is no signal yet,
 * explicitly so callers "fall back to generic text rather than claiming false
 * precision". So this reads the real status and the real step, and where it has
 * nothing to report it says something honest instead of inventing a percentage.
 *
 * What IS kept from the design: the mark you just bought held up at full size
 * with the rings travelling out from it, because the wait is the moment the
 * purchase feels real.
 */

export type Phase = "working" | "ready" | "error";

/* The stage list MIRRORS worker/index.ts's real checkpoints, in the order it
   reaches them. Each `key` is a distinct substring of the label the worker
   actually writes to `Server.provisioningStep`:

     "Allocating your server…"        line 590
     "Configuring the network…"       line 620
     "Starting your server…"          line 751
     "Booting the operating system…"  line 763   (skipped under NXEON_SANDBOX)
     "Waiting for network access…"    line 788
     "Starting the game server…"      line 806   (game orders only)

   THIS LIST IS A CONTRACT WITH THE WORKER. It previously carried the design
   sandbox's invented journey — "Installing the image", "Applying security",
   "Finalising setup" — none of which the worker has ever written, while two
   checkpoints it does write matched nothing. In production that meant the
   screen lit up for the first two steps and then fell back to "no signal",
   hiding the progress bar mid-provision. If you add a `step()` call to the
   worker, add its row here; if you rename one, rename the key.

   "Starting your server" and "Starting the game server" both contain
   "starting", so the keys are long enough to tell them apart. */
const STAGES: { key: string; label: string; sub: string; icon: string; gameOnly?: boolean }[] = [
  { key: "allocating", label: "Allocating resources", sub: "Reserving CPU, memory and storage", icon: "cpu" },
  { key: "configuring the network", label: "Configuring network", sub: "Assigning the address and routes", icon: "nodes" },
  { key: "starting your server", label: "Starting the machine", sub: "Powering on your server", icon: "bolt" },
  { key: "booting", label: "Booting the image", sub: "Bringing up the operating system", icon: "download" },
  { key: "waiting for network", label: "Waiting for network", sub: "Confirming it is reachable", icon: "globe2" },
  { key: "starting the game server", label: "Starting the game", sub: "Opening the port to players", icon: "gamepad", gameOnly: true },
  /* LAST, and game-only. `waitOutGameInstall` writes this AFTER the container is
     up (worker/index.ts:1010, called past the "Starting the game server" step),
     because the game itself is still downloading — tens of gigabytes for some
     families. It was added on main in 08a16a1, which stopped healthy servers
     being declared failed for taking a long time over a big install; without a

### Shared hosting dashboard — `components/customer/hosting/v2/`
Full rebuild, replacing `HostingTabs.tsx` and its twelve sibling panels (all
deleted). Hero with the customer's actual website on the left, plan identity and
five plan ceilings on the right; ten tabs; Overview as a bento of Websites →
HTTPS → Storage → Subscription → Activity.

- **The redundancy the owner reported was real.** The old Overview rendered, at
  once, on a healthy account: an SFTP strip, an App-credentials card, a "Your
  account is ready — here's how to go live" checklist whose first step was
  *Install WordPress*, and a task feed reading "WordPress installed". On top of
  that, `<Provisioning/>` was rendered **unconditionally** (the VPS page gates it
  on `transitional || purchase=1 || ERROR`), so every visit opened with a
  full-width "Your hosting is ready ✓ · Open the panel". All four are fixed at
  the source: setup steps are measured facts that stop being true, app logins
  live on the website they belong to, the feed became the Activity tab, and the
  overlay is gated like the VPS one.
- **Plan vs website** is the organising idea. The plan owns every limit; a
  website owns an environment (address, certificate, docroot, app). Each website
  has its own dashboard with its own file browser rooted at its own docroot.
- **Files reuse the real file manager.** `components/customer/files/FileBrowser`
  now takes a `FileApi` adapter (`lib/files-adapters.ts`) — `serverFileApi` for a
  VPS, `hostingFileApi` for a hosting account — so hosting gets the identical
  three-pane browser, lazy tree and XHR upload queue rather than a second one.
- **Folder-scoped SFTP logins** (`HostingFtpUser`, `MAX_FTP_USERS = 8`). Real
  enforcement: a unix user plus an sshd `Match User … ChrootDirectory` block
  (`taskCreateFtpUser`), `sshd -t`-guarded exactly like the account's own chroot;
  read-only logins are left out of the account's group so POSIX refuses writes.
  A per-site container is re-owned `root:<account> 0750` first, because sshd
  refuses a chroot any non-root user can write — the docroot inside is untouched,
  so PHP keeps writing. **Never verified against a real node** (this fork has
  none, and touching a production node was out of scope).
- **Website previews are captured for real** — `lib/hosting-thumb.ts` launches
  headless Chromium against the site's public hostname. Verified end to end:
  `example.com` → a 17 KB JPEG; a hostname resolving to a private address is
  refused (SSRF guard). Three sources, always labelled: capture / upload /
  placeholder. A failed capture stores the reason and the card shows it.
- **Storage add-on post-deploy** (`expandHostingStorage`) — extra storage could
  previously only be bought at order time. Same money path and same
  `lib/extra-disk.ts` helpers as the VPS control, which is reused directly.
- **Not measured, so not drawn:** bandwidth (nginx traffic is not attributed per
  account — the allowance is shown with the reason), mailbox count before the
  bundled subscription exists, backup download (no route streams one out).

content.text:
The Shared Hosting Dashboard is rebuilt, deployed and verified in both themes. Report follows.

## What was built

**New surface:** `components/customer/hosting/v2/` (20 files, ~4,100 lines) wired in from `app/dashboard/hosting/[id]/page.tsx`. The old path is **deleted**, not left alongside: `HostingTabs.tsx` plus `WebsitesPanel`, `FileManager`, `Backups`, `CronPanel`, `EmailTab`, `SubdomainsPanel`, `AddonDomainsPanel`, `AppInstaller`, `AppCredentials`, `PhpSwitcher`, `PlanUpgrade`, `shared.tsx`, `DatabasesPanel` are gone. `DbManager.tsx` (DB Studio) survives and is mounted as-is.

Visual foundation is the VPS v2 kit imported directly (`vpspanel/v2/kit`, `ui`, `VpsStorageMeter`) — no second dialect. Everything uses `text-tx*` / `border-rim-*` / `bg-well` tokens; `.nx-dark-island` only on the photographic preview frames.

### Hero
Website preview left (16:10), plan identity right: plan name + real `planSlug` tag, primary domain, PHP version, status, renewal price on the sold term, SFTP host/username chips, **Upgrade plan**. Five ceilings as `used / limit` with bars: Websites 3/11 · Storage 5.5 GB/20 GB · Bandwidth · Email · Databases 2/25.

### Overview
Setup card (only while something is genuinely outstanding) → Websites grid (3-up, thumbnail + domain + status + app icon + View more + dotted **Add website**) → HTTPS · Storage breakdown · Subscription → Recent activity.

### Other tabs
Websites (grid → per-site dashboard with its own Overview/Files/Database/Apps/Settings), Files, Databases, Email, Apps, Cron, Backups, Activity, Settings.

## Backend built (not mocked)

| Feature | Real capability |
|---|---|
| **Website screenshots** | `lib/hosting-thumb.ts` — headless Chromium via a `CAPTURE_SITE_THUMB` HostingTask. **Verified end to end**: `example.com` → a real 17,320-byte JPEG; a hostname resolving to a private address is refused (SSRF guard). Bytes on `HostingSiteThumb`, served by `app/api/hosting/thumb`. Three sources, each labelled on the card (capture / upload / placeholder); a failure stores its reason and the card shows it. |
| **Custom thumbnails** | Upload through the same route, validated by the platform's existing signature-sniffing image validator (no SVG). |
| **Scoped FTP logins** | New `HostingFtpUser` + 3 task kinds + `taskCreateFtpUser/Delete/Reset`. Real mechanism: a unix user plus an sshd `Match User … ChrootDirectory` block, `sshd -t`-guarded exactly like the account's own chroot; read-only logins are left out of the account's group so POSIX refuses writes. Per-site container re-owned `root:<account> 0750` first (sshd refuses a chroot a non-root user can write) — the docroot inside is untouched so PHP keeps writing. **Verified through the UI**: created `nxcustomer462c05-designer` scoped to `subdomains/shop`, PENDING → ACTIVE. |
| **Post-deploy storage** | `expandHostingStorage` — same money path and same `lib/extra-disk.ts` helpers as VPS, reusing `VpsStorageMeter` itself. Previously extra storage could **only** be bought at order time. |
| **Storage breakdown** | `hostingUsageSweep` now writes a per-directory `du -sm` in the same pass as the total, into `HostingAccount.usageBreakdown`. Null = no reading, and the card says why. |
| **Files** | `FileBrowser`/`UploadQueue` refactored to a `FileApi` adapter (`lib/files-adapters.ts`). Hosting gets the *identical* VPS component — tree, search, sorting, multi-select, editor, XHR byte-progress uploads. Per-website views are rooted at that site's docroot. |

## The redundancy you reported — root causes, fixed at source

1. `<Provisioning/>` was rendered **unconditionally** (the VPS page gates it on `transitional \|\| purchase=1 \|\| ERROR`), so every visit to a healthy account opened with "Your hosting is ready ✓ · Open the panel". Now gated identically.
2. `GettingStarted` always rendered with *Install WordPress* as step 1. Replaced by a card whose every step is a measured fact that stops being true; it disappears entirely when they all do.
3. `AppCredentials` sat on the plan Overview. Moved onto the website the app was installed on.
4. `TaskFeed` printed the WordPress admin password inline, duplicating (3). Became the Activity tab; no credential in it.
5. SFTP was a grey strip mid-Overview with no port or protocol. Now Settings → Access.

## Scoped down / honest gaps

- **Bandwidth is not metered per account** anywhere in the platform. The tile shows the allowance and says why, rather than the "200 GB / 1 TB" the brief asked for. Real work: attribute nginx `body_bytes_sent` per vhost in the node telemetry shipper.
- **Per-website database isolation does not exist** and I did not imply it does. All sites share one unix user, one FPM pool and one account-scoped MySQL grant. I added `HostingDatabase.siteKey` as a customer-set *assignment*, and both the per-site and plan-level Database cards state the limitation explicitly. Filesystem separation **is** real and is what the scoped FTP logins enforce.
- **Free Nxeon subdomain per website** — the backend's `createSubdomain` makes `<label>.<primaryDomain>`, not a fresh `x.sites.nxeon.cloud`. The Add-website form offers exactly what works.
- **FTP chroot is unverified against a real node** — this fork has none and touching production was out of scope. Design rationale is documented in `taskCreateFtpUser`; a staging node run is wanted before selling it.
- **Backup download** still doesn't exist (archives are root-owned on the node); the card says so instead of offering a dead button.
- **Tab order** deviates from your enumeration: Settings sits last rather than between Activity and Email, matching every other panel's "daily work first, configuration last". Domains is folded into Websites.

## DB Studio — gap analysis

MySQL/MariaDB only (`HostingDatabase` has no engine field; Postgres exists only for VPS, Mongo nowhere). Security model is sound — grant-as-boundary, `?`-bound values, identifiers validated against live `SHOW TABLES`, no injection found.

**Has:** table tree, overview (rows/data/index/engine/collation), browse with paging + sort + per-column filters + global search + bulk delete, inline edit, row editor, SQL tab with history, structure (columns/indexes/`SHOW CREATE`), add/drop column, add/drop index, truncate/drop/rename/optimize, import (≤512 KB, ≤200 statements), per-table SQL/CSV export.

**Missing:** create table · modify/rename column · foreign keys · views/triggers/routines · whole-database export · drop database · DB users & grants · EXPLAIN · saved queries · multi-statement SQL · charset/collation/engine changes · phpMyAdmin-style Search tab.

**Bugs found — four fixed in this pass:**
- Structure tab headed a column "Collation" and rendered the *comment* in it; the collation field was never read. → both now read and shown.
- Exports silently truncated at 1,000 rows, CSV with no marker at all. → blocking confirmation + the filename now says `table.first-1000-rows.csv`.
- Row counts (InnoDB estimates) shown bare. → `~` prefix and "Rows (approx)" header.
- Sandbox returned invented tables/counts through the normal UI. → "demo data" badge + banner.

**Left for you to fund (highest value first):** export the SQL tab's results (S) · list views (S) · bulk delete in one statement instead of N round-trips (S) · **create table form** (M — the #1 beginner task, currently impossible without hand-written DDL) · full-database export + a streaming download route (M) · modify column (M — today changing a column means drop+re-add, which destroys data) · binary/BLOB handling, currently `Buffer.toString("utf8")` and silently corrupting (M) · **connection reuse** (L — fixes both the 7-SSH-connections-per-click latency *and* the fact that `SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0` silently no-ops during import, which means Studio's own dumps can't be re-imported) · **a real import pipeline** (L — an 8 MB WordPress dump is currently unimportable, the single biggest reason to leave for a host with phpMyAdmin).

Also flagged: no `deleteHostingDatabase` action exists anywhere, and backups can't be downloaded — so a customer has **no supported way to get a complete copy of their own database**. That's a retention/portability problem, not just a feature gap.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `./rebuild.sh` green; screenshot passes in **both themes** across Overview, Websites, website detail, Files, Databases, Apps, Cron, Settings→Access and Settings→Storage. Three light-theme contrast issues found and fixed by looking at the images (setup CTAs, DB Studio banner, a double-rendered field label), plus a wrong back-chevron glyph.

A sandbox demo seeder is at `scripts/seed-hosting-demo.ts` (refuses to run without `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`) — every hosting account on node-2 was `PENDING`, so there was nothing to render. `docs/NEXION-V2.md` has a new section covering all of the above.
